author: agent
text:
FULL RE-RANK — all four bands, impact rubric applied end to end.

Distribution: S0=7 S1=14 S2=25 S3=26 (72 open). S0 share 9%, inside the 1-in-5 calibration guard.

S0 (7) — credential asserts something never established, or a real credential is handed out:
  .30 unverified JWT payload -> IAA2 'IdP-verified'
  .49 merely-connected device -> IAA3 + Hardware presence
  .47 presence gate read from audience[0], token signed for all audiences
  .71 unrecognised presence requirement drops to None; gate can never fail
  .41 root identity to every consumer; pseudonymity and peer attestation unwired
  .55 PROMOTED. attacker-chosen authority. Verified chain: oidc.rs:80-88 takes iss from the
      unverified JWT (.30), extract_domain() -> TrustDomain::OrgOidc(domain), and
      SpiffeId::uri() interpolates it as the authority in format!("spiffe://{}/{}").
      Whoever can drop a token in the cache picks the trust domain of the issued SVID.
  .105 PROMOTED. OidcCachedAttestor::prove hands the caller a live IdP bearer token and
      ignores the challenge. With .41 (no peer attestation) any local process can ask.
      This is not a false claim, it is the user's real credential leaving the daemon.

Notable demotions, with reasons:
  .10 .11 CI breakage, not a defect in shipped behaviour -> S2
  .28 .38 panics behind unusual preconditions (non-UTF8 path, poisoned lock) -> S2
  .39 zeroization of an already-ephemeral, process-lifetime key -> S2 hardening
  .52 pseudonym scheme version is future-proofing, nothing is wrong today -> S2
  .25 .54 pre-1.0 API hygiene, breaking changes still free -> S3
  .15 .18 .32 .64 .65 .88 API ergonomics and test flake -> S3

One promotion out of S3: .29, OIDC freshness() encodes token expiry in the assurance level,
so a consumer reading assurance gets a value that means something else.

Checked and left alone: .40 (chrono_timestamp drops the date) reads as a claims bug but is
persona/src/main.rs:475, CLI display only, never in the credential path. Stays S3.
.79 (GPG subkey fingerprint) held at S1 rather than promoted: the derived id is wrong but
stable and unique to the user, so it mislabels rather than enables impersonation - it does
not outrank .49.

Method note: ranks below S0 were set from titles plus session context, not a re-read of all
72 descriptions. The S0 band and every band-crossing move above was verified against source.
